title: Room visibility, directory and self-join (org-public or private), with a late-joiner history rule
summary: Add open/private visibility to named rooms in Control, a paged directory of org-public rooms the caller is not in (member count, description), and a self-join decision that grants exactly room membership with the default role; private rooms return not-found to non-members. Record join and leave sequence per membership so thread reads can be limited to a tenure window, and make membership-change and revocation delivery durable. Self-join must never widen the ACL on documents bound to the room.
whyItMatters: Browse and join is table stakes in buzz, Slack and Teams; today a person sees only rooms they were added to. Control already stores a privacy_revision to build on.

others: qm (tri-state membership, deny-on-unknown fallback; sequence-bounded participant windows)
slack (public and private channels, no record in this category)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-02] 3 of 5 for discovery and self-join (buzz, teams, qm); tenure windows 1 of 5 (qm); table-stakes for discovery, unique for tenure [R-t1-04-05] 3 of 5 sources; table-stakes (Slack evidence is DOC only; buzz open channel directory is SRC)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-02] room.visibility in {open, private}. GET /rooms/directory returns open rooms in the org the caller is not in, paged and separate from the member poll. POST /rooms/{id}/join self-grants the default role only for open rooms; private rooms 404 to non-members; when membership is unknown, deny. QM adds ParticipantWindow{validFromSeq, validToSeq} on membership rows that filters transcript reads and approvals, and a roster-version fence on enqueue. [R-t1-04-05] Rooms carry visibility (public or private); the directory lists public rooms in the org with member count and description; join is a self-add membership allowed only for public rooms; an external directory lists cross-org connections with status (pending, active).

Fencing by authority and audience revision is strong, but late-joiner history and durable delivery of revocations are not covered. [R-t1-04-05] Space listing is filtered to the caller's Control index (spaces.rs:2747-2810). A grep in this step found only an is_organization_room flag (the org's own room, pinned in the sidebar) and no visibility field under Control Plane user-core/internal/spaces, so there is no public visibility, browse route or self-join route.

approachOriginal: [R-t1-02-02] Control Plane (user-core): add visibility to registered_spaces (bump privacy_revision on change) and a self-join decision that writes a membership only for open rooms and org members, keeping thread_read_entitled and the owner-plane knowledge ACL in force. Store join and leave sequence per membership and carry the reader's window in the thread-read decision (shared_thread_read_decision.go) so Session Core filters transcripts; make the history rule a room setting (full history default for open rooms, strict window default for guests). Application Plane: mirror visibility on spaces and add a directory query separate from the member list. Gateway: GET /api/v1/spaces/directory, POST /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/join. Frontend: browse dialog in CoreSidebarSpacesPanel. Move membership_changed to JetStream or an outbox. [R-t1-04-05] Control Plane (user-core spaces): add visibility to the Space record and a self-join decision that adds the caller as a member of an org-public Space and nothing else; bound documents keep their own owner-plane ACL checks. Gateway: GET browse route returning only org-public Spaces of the caller's active org. Frontend: directory page with search by name and a Join button. Membership changes must propagate to Session Core reliably.
dependencies: Room role management (F-t1-022 (R-t1-02-01)) for the default join role

Reliable membership-change propagation to Session Core (today plain, lossy NATS)

risks: [R-t1-02-02] A self-joiner could read history from before they joined; decide the tenure rule first (Slack shows full history, QM windows strictly). Open-room names in the directory must respect residency and ZDR. Self-join must never widen an owner-plane ACL, so the knowledge intersection still applies after join. [R-t1-04-05] A public room with bound documents may look like it grants document access; the UI must show that documents stay owner-ACL gated. Joining a room must never widen an owner-plane ACL.

verevon.exactGap: No visibility, directory, self-join or tenure rule exists (SRC): registered_spaces has no visibility column (privacy_revision is only a revision counter), space_memberships has no valid_from or join sequence, the gateway route table has no browse or join route, and the sidebar and listing show only Spaces in the caller Control index (a non-member already gets 404, so private-by-membership is today the only mode). Session Core applies only a recipient-audience-revision ceiling to shared-thread reads (rows newer than the reader decision are dropped), never a floor, so any current member reads the full history. membership_changed is published by user-core through JetStream fire-and-forget (errors only logged, no outbox) and consumed by session-core with a plain NATS subscribe by design, so a missed event is never replayed; the item text says "plain NATS" for the publisher, which is slightly off.

session-core audience-ceiling filter on messages and threads (basis for a floor, see approach)
Control ReplaceMemberships and the Application intent record for the membership write
verevon.constraints: ADR-0001 (SRC): Application owns Space name, kind and lifecycle; Control owns membership, privacy decisions and revisions, so visibility belongs in Control and name or description in Application, and the directory must compose both in the gateway as the index already does. Membership writes today are an Application declarative full replace into Control (ReplaceMemberships deactivates managed users not declared, spaceMembers.ts:243), so a Control-native self-join would be revoked at the next sync of that room unless the self-join goes through the Application intent record or the sync is scoped by source (INF from SRC). Product intent is that team and external Spaces are visible only to explicit participants (SRC UI research doc), so org-public rooms are a deliberate Slack-style policy change: private by default and opt-in per org. Never widen an owner-plane ACL on join (ADR-0001). Room names in the directory must respect residency and ZDR. The tenure window needs a join marker: the existing per-message recipient_audience_revision stamp is a candidate floor (INF, low confidence, not traced through Application audience registration).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: membership_changed already goes out over JetStream; the non-durable part is the plain-subscribe consumer in session-core (by design) and the absence of a publisher outbox. For self-join, pick the membership writer first (Application intent record versus Control source-tagged writes) and keep rooms private by default with org-public opt-in. Default the history rule to full history for open rooms, which is today behaviour and costs nothing, and defer the strict tenure floor to the guest work (F-t1-053). Split the item: visibility, directory and join is M; tenure window and durable delivery are the L part.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged at L, but recommend splitting; the visibility, directory and join slice alone is M once the membership writer is decided.
verevon.verdictReason: Absence confirmed and the feature is table stakes, but the approach must resolve who writes room membership (declarative Application sync would clobber a Control self-join) and fix the NATS description.

title: Searchable people-and-agent directory with an agent-readable resolver
summary: Add a Control Plane directory search (org members and registered agents by name or email prefix) that returns only subjects the caller may see, expose it through the gateway to the add-member and DM pickers, and give agents a resolve tool that answers ok, ambiguous (with candidates) or none (with a reason).
whyItMatters: Needed to add members, start DMs and group rooms (Teams-like team support) and for agents to address the right human. All five references have it; Verevon has per-Space rosters and an org member list but nothing searchable across the org.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One picker resolves org directory, saved contacts and external users (external found only by exact email/SIP to prevent enumeration), with guest/external tags and chat/call/block actions; results ranked by recent interaction. qm adds resolver vocabulary for agents: ok, ambiguous, none, not-in-channel, unlinked login.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: A per-Space roster (person or agent kind, role) and an org member list exist. There is no searchable directory across the org or Spaces (a grep for directory or member-search routes in gateway orgs/ found none), no external or guest lookup, no contact actions, and no resolver with agent-readable errors.

approachOriginal: Control Plane (identity owner): GET /orgs/{id}/directory/search (name/email prefix, people and agents) returning only subjects visible to the caller; external lookup by exact email once external access exists. Gateway exposes it to pickers and to an agent resolve tool returning ok|ambiguous|none. Frontend: shared picker component used by add-member, DM start and the @ menu.
dependencies: DMs, group rooms and guest model (other audit categories)
risks: Directory enumeration across orgs; agents resolving to the wrong person.

verevon.exactGap: People side (SRC): org-core already serves GET /orgs/:id/members/search (name or email substring, active plus invited members, max 20 results, max 50 profile fetches), but the gateway never proxies it and nothing in the SPA calls it; the add-member picker instead lists every active org member from the gateway list_members route with no search box. Agent side (SRC): an org-wide agent registry already exists in the Application Plane (agentInstallationsForOrgForGateway, gateway GET /api/v1/agents/installations, ADR-0002, a presence-not-authority label surface) and the composer builds @-candidates from Space roster plus bound agents only, but nothing merges people and agents, and no agent-callable resolver returning ok/ambiguous/none exists in Model, Application or Control code (INF, from a negative grep of resolve_/lookup_/find_ patterns). The DM, group-room and guest targets the item names do not exist yet (Space kind is only personal/room/project/case), so a DM picker has no consumer today.
reuse: org-core searchMembers handler and MemberSuggestion type (restrict to active members before exposing)
gateway orgs/members.rs list_members (auth-core list-members, already returns name and email)
Application registry: Convex agentInstallationsForOrgForGateway and gateway list_org_agent_installations (ADR-0002)
SpaceRoomComposer MentionCandidate model (person|agent) and the Control RosterMember shape (subject_type user|service)
gateway authorized_org_id pattern so the org always comes from the session, never from the client
verevon.constraints: Plane ownership (SRC): people identity is auth-core/org-core (Auth Core is the sole membership authority); the cross-Space agent registry is owned by the Application Plane per ADR-0002, so a Control-owned combined directory conflicts with that ADR for the agent half. ADR-0002 says the registry answers presence, not authority: a resolver result must never imply the caller may invoke the agent, which still needs Control roster/decision for the specific Space. org-core members/search is service-authenticated with no per-user delegation and also returns invited emails, so it must be exposed only through the gateway with the session org and active-only filtering. Cross-org or external lookup needs the cross-org identity and privacy contract the UI research doc requires (SRC: VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md:128-132), so it must wait for F-t1-053. ZDR is not affected (names and emails only). The default ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT is 100 (SRC auth.ts:953-956), so client-side filtering of the existing list is enough at default scale.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not make Control the directory owner for agents. Slice 1 (S): add a search field to the existing add-member picker, or expose org-core members/search through a gateway route that forces the session org and returns active members only. Slice 2 (M): compose people (org-core/auth-core) and agents (Application registry) in the gateway, and expose the ok|ambiguous|none resolver as an agent tool through the gateway/capability path with presence-not-authority semantics. Defer external and guest lookup to the guest model.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall, but the people-search slice is S because org-core search and the roster list already exist; the agent resolver tool is the M part.
verevon.verdictReason: Recommendation is valid but two premises are wrong: a people search already exists in org-core (just unexposed and with an invited-email leak), and the plane owner for the agent half is the Application Plane (ADR-0002), not Control. Also depends on DMs and guests that do not exist.

title: Meeting intelligence with consent: long-form transcription and an authority-scoped recap saved as a Space document, under a deny-by-default per-meeting AI policy
summary: Build the meeting-intelligence MVP from uploaded recordings first, then live calls: long-form speech-to-text with speaker labels and timestamps in the Model Plane, transcript segments stored as Data Plane knowledge units (not room posts), and a recap (decisions, action items with owners, chapters, citations to segments) written back as an editable Space document. Gate it with a Control-owned per-meeting policy {ai_access off|transcript_only|full, privacy_mode, ephemeral or retained answers, managers, locked fields} checked before any ASR, agent or recap reads audio or transcript, announced to all participants, default-off when externals are present.
whyItMatters: Transcript and AI recap are table stakes in Teams, Slack and buzz, and the meeting-intelligence design (a meeting as a source type on existing retrieval, wiki and ZDR rails) is architecturally sound but has no code. Teams' consent controls must ship with it, not after.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (REA): recap with notes, tasks, topics, chapters, speaker timeline, citations back to the recording and visibility derived from transcript access; Teams (REA): visible AI on/off, privacy mode that blocks Copilot and all agents, ephemeral versus retained answers by org policy, only selected people can change AI settings, admin-locked options shown as locked
others: Slack (DOC): notes become a canvas in the huddle
Buzz (SRC): transcript segments are ordinary chat messages in the meeting channel
Slack (DOC): announce to all when AI notes start, default off with external guests
Grok Bot (SRC, medium): per-meeting or blanket consent card for the agent and an admin visibility setting (MANAGERS or EVERYONE)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-03-02] 3 of 5 (Buzz, Slack, Teams); table-stakes. Citations, attendance report and content-bin report are Teams-only. [R-t1-03-03] 2 of 5 (Teams, Slack) for AI policy, differentiator; Grok Bot adds consent for agent attendance; admin-locked indicator is Teams-only.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-03-02] Audio to streaming or batch ASR with diarisation produces segments {speaker, t_start, t_end, text}; on meeting end a reasoning pass produces the recap with citations to segments; the recap is saved as an editable document or canvas in the room; action items become tasks only after human approval; recap visibility equals transcript visibility (no transcript access, no AI summary); attendance comes from roster events. [R-t1-03-03] Policy evaluated server-side before any agent or ASR reads meeting content. Enabling AI emits a system message to participants and a badge. Externals present means default off. Ephemeral answers are stored with a meeting-scoped TTL. Fields locked by an admin render as locked with the owner of the lock.

Control Plane: private-until-shared visibility with attendees as the default audience and the this item (R-t1-03-03) policy as precondition. Enforcement sits on the data: transcript and recap knowledge units carry the policy revision so retrieval cannot leak them through a chat copy. Ephemeral answers use a meeting-scoped TTL. title: Retention policies for rooms, files and agent sessions, plus shared-Space deletion on the existing saga
summary: Add org and per-Space retention policies (keep, N days, ZDR) carried in Control's signed decision and enforced by per-plane sweepers that reuse the per-plane receipts of the Space deletion saga: room projections, Model Plane threads, messages and agent memory, sandbox-manager workspaces and process output, Data Plane documents bound to the Space, and notification feeds. Extend the saga from personal Spaces to shared Spaces with owner approval and write fencing. Legal hold overrides retention.
whyItMatters: Retention is a gating enterprise question and a GDPR storage-limitation duty. Verevon has the hardest part already (cross-plane receipts, legal hold) but only for personal Space deletion, and nothing between keep-forever and ZDR.

others: teams (preserves edited and deleted originals in hidden compliance stores)
buzz (durable deletion engine with approvals and checkpoints)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Retention: 3 of 5 (slack, teams, buzz doc); durable shared-space deletion: 1 of 5 (buzz). Common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Policy objects at org, workspace, channel and DM scope; the most specific wins unless the org locks it, with a member override for private rooms. A scheduled sweeper deletes expired items across stores via deletion receipts; policy changes are audited and may need owner approval. Deletion: request, frozen inventory digest, owner approval, write fence, resumable executor with checkpoints, abortable until destruction starts, final receipt.

Application Plane: a sweeper over room projections that writes per-plane deletion receipts using the existing spaceDeletionOwnerReceipts schema and reconciler; each owner plane (session-core, agent_memory, sandbox-manager, Data Plane, notification feed) accepts a purge-before request. title: Typed timeline entries: server-signed system messages, a card registry with a safe fallback, link previews through Quarry, and pointer embeds for artifacts
summary: Give Session Core entries a content_type plus payload, render by type through a card registry with a neutral unsupported-update fallback, and let the server emit typed system entries from Control and Application events (member added or removed, agent bound or paused, rename, history window). Add link previews fetched by Quarry with SSRF guards and stored as a snapshot so recipients never contact the third-party site, provider link cards classified in the browser, and an embed block that stores only {kind, id} for a canvas, list, record or file and renders it under the viewer's own grant with a request-access stub.
whyItMatters: Teams has 87+ typed system notices including agent added or removed, and buzz signs notices so clients cannot forge them; Verevon shows membership and binding changes only in a separate Activity tab. Pointer embeds keep artifacts under their own ACL instead of copying content into messages.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (typed previews with unknown and retired fallback cards); teams (87+ typed system notices incl. agent added or removed); buzz (relay-signed notices, sender-side link snapshots); Teams Loop (REA) for pointer embeds with their own ACL and a sharing warning; Grok Bot (SRC) for provider link-card classification
others: Slack typed cloud pickers as hardened child windows (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-10] Typed content 2 of 5 and system messages 2 of 5 (differentiators); link previews 3 of 5 (common) [R-t1-08-10] pointer embeds: 1 of 5, unique; provider cards and pickers: 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-10] Entry {content_type enum, payload oneof}; the preview projection is typed; the client renders a fallback card for unknown types and logs once per type. System entries {type, actor, subject, details} are emitted by the server from authority events and are never client-authored (buzz signs them with the relay key). Link preview: the sender side fetches under SSRF guards (private-IP block, redirect cap, 256 KB page and 2 MB image caps, per-host cooldown), extracts OG metadata, re-hosts a sanitized image and stores a signed snapshot with the message; recipients never contact the third-party site. Slack lets apps enrich unfurls. [R-t1-08-10] Message body contains an embed {artifact_kind, artifact_id}; the renderer fetches the artifact under the viewer's grant and subscribes to live updates; a viewer without access sees a request-access stub; pasting elsewhere reuses the same id; the share dialog warns when posting to an audience wider than the artifact ACL. Link cards use host-pattern to provider and path-pattern to kind tables and never fetch content.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: [R-t1-01-10] AppendMessageRequest carries role (user, assistant, system, tool), content and a metadata struct but no content_type; room posts render as markdown or plain text. Membership, grants and receipts appear in the separate Activity tab, not in the room timeline (checked in features/spaces: no member-added or agent-bound timeline rows). No link previews. Baseline had no record for typed content or system entries, so a final check of Session Core message conventions is still needed. [R-t1-08-10] Room posts cannot embed any artifact (chat artifacts are inline SSE payloads, not pointers to an independently authorized object). No link previews or provider cards in rooms; the baseline recorded attachments and link previews as absent in the room, and the integration-core provider actions are not offered as a picker (not re-verified).

approachOriginal: [R-t1-01-10] Model Plane proto: add content_type and a payload oneof (or a namespaced metadata.kind as an interim to avoid a breaking migration); existing rows default to text. Application Plane: project Control membership and binding events and Space lifecycle events into typed system entries appended under a server-only decision (clients cannot author them). Frontend: card registry (text, system notice, approval card, receipt, file, link preview, unknown fallback). Ingestion Plane: a Quarry fetch-preview endpoint (private-IP block, redirect cap, 256 KB and 2 MB caps, OG extract, re-hosted sanitized image) called by the gateway at send; snapshot stored on the entry; integration-corev2 providers can later supply richer unfurls. ZDR orgs may disable previews. Coordinate with category 12 (C-t1-12-012 typed transcript rows) and category 06 (C-t1-06-027 unfurling). [R-t1-08-10] Frontend Plane: an embed block type in room messages rendering canvas, list, record and file cards by id through the gateway under the viewer's decision; a pure client-side URL classifier for provider cards; pickers later through Ingestion integration-corev2 OAuth grants that never widen the owner ACL. Application Plane live updates reuse the existing realtime projection. Adopt the embed format inside the canvas and lists work, not as a separate product.
dependencies: Control and Application event feeds for membership and agent binding
planeOwner: Model Plane (entry schema) with Application Plane (system projection), Ingestion Plane (Quarry preview) and Frontend Plane (card registry)
risks: [R-t1-01-10] Schema migration of existing turns. Event-to-timeline consistency. SSRF and tracking-pixel leakage in previews; preview snapshots under ZDR; titles of private pages leaking through external unfurls. A decision card must not be confused with a Control approval of an effect. [R-t1-08-10] N+1 fetches on long timelines. A request-access stub must not leak titles or metadata to unauthorized viewers. Server-side unfurl would leak URLs, so keep classification client-side.

verevon.exactGap: AppendMessageRequest carries role, content and an opaque metadata Struct but no content_type, and the room timeline normalizes transcripts to user and assistant turns only (normalizeTranscriptTurns drops every other role) rendered as markdown or plain text, with the approval panel as the only inline typed card; typed rendering exists only in the Activity tab (ActivityRenderClass and lenses). There are no member-added, agent-bound or rename rows in the timeline or in Activity (activity-grammar has no membership class), no link previews and no pointer embeds; Quarry has an SSRF guard (dns_guard) and OpenGraph extraction and the gateway has a render-based scrape-preview route, but no light metadata-only fetch-preview endpoint.

The room is a list of thread-posts (each a Session Core thread), not one continuous timeline, so membership and agent-state notices have no thread to live in. The gateway never dials third-party URLs (it forwards to Quarry), previews must be snapshots stored at send so recipients never contact the site, and ZDR rooms disable previews and snapshots. title: Guests and link invitations with mandatory expiry
summary: Introduce a guest principal type with memberships only in explicitly granted rooms, no directory or roster access and no agent invocation by default, invited through room-scoped invitations with a required expiry. Extend invitations with shareable links or codes (TTL, max uses, optional admin approval, stored terms acceptance) and a combined invite-to-org-and-room flow.
whyItMatters: Teams, Slack, QM and Buzz all support external collaborators; Verevon rosters only active org members, so a customer or contractor cannot be pulled into one room. Org invitations exist but cannot target a room or be shared as a link.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (guest tiers), buzz (invite codes), qm (mandatory guest expiry)
others: slack (single- vs multi-channel guests, admin approval queue)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: principal.type in {internal, guest}. Guests get memberships only in granted rooms, cannot browse the directory, create rooms or see the roster, and by default cannot invoke agents; invitations require expires_at and expiry removes memberships through the normal membership-change path. Invite code = base64(org, room?, role, expires_at, max_uses, nonce) + HMAC; claim verifies HMAC and expiry, counts uses, records terms acceptance, then creates the membership through the normal Control path; claim is rate-limited (10 per minute in Buzz).

apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/auth.ts:942-960 (org email invitations, 48 h, verified email, rate-limited accept)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceMembers.ts:60-73 (a room grant requires existing org membership by design)
verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Org email invitations exist, but there are no guests, no room-scoped invitations, no link or code invites with max uses, no approval queue, and no stored terms acceptance.

approachOriginal: Control Plane (auth-core, org-core, user-core): guest principal type, room-scoped guest invitation with mandatory expiry, and link invites with TTL, max uses and an optional room target and role; per-org approval policy. Agent turns in rooms with guests use the room audience in the Control decision so org-only knowledge is not retrieved. Guest seats flow to billing-core. Frontend: invite dialog on the room with a link option.
risks: Agent answers in a guest room can leak org knowledge; guest seat billing; ZDR and residency apply to guest data too; link invites leak easily, so keep a short TTL, max uses and admin revoke.

verevon.exactGap: Only org-level email invitations exist (SRC): the Better Auth organization plugin in auth-core with a 48 h default expiry, email-verification requirement and a rate-limited accept route, and a gateway invite limited to member/admin roles; invitation rows carry an unused teamId column and the auth event publishes an empty inviteCode. There is no guest principal (Control space_memberships only allows user or service subjects; Application room grants require an existing active org member and are hard-coded to role editor), no room-scoped invitation, no link or code invite with max uses, no approval queue and no stored terms acceptance. The product docs also state that external access needs its own cross-org identity and privacy contract before any invite list (SRC: VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md:128-132).
reuse: Better Auth invitation table and flow in auth-core (expiresAt already mandatory, status, inviterId; add a room target and a token for link invites)
sendInvitationEmail/buildInvitationLink and AcceptInvitationPage plus the accept-invitation rate limit
Control recipient-audience and Space decision machinery as the fence that keeps org-only knowledge out of guest rooms (ADR-0001 intersection rule)
org-core roles already include viewer at the service level (handlers.go:483), although the gateway only allows member/admin
billing-core seat concept (not opened in this audit; verify before relying on it)
verevon.constraints: Auth Core is the sole org-membership authority (SRC: org-core/internal/http/server.go:122-128 comment), so guest identity belongs in auth-core, not in Application. A guest must NOT become a plain org member (INF): org-visible documents and the organization-room roster sync would then include them. Room membership writes today flow Application spaceMemberGrants -> declarative PUT to Control, and ReplaceMemberships revokes any managed (user) member not in the declared list (SRC repository.go:744-775), so a Control-created guest membership of subject_type user would be revoked on the next sync unless the guest uses a distinct subject_type or the sync is scoped by source. Control space_memberships CHECK allows only user and service (SRC 017 migration line 62). Agent turns in a guest room must use the room recipient audience so retrieval is narrowed (ADR-0001); I did not trace that Data Plane honors the audience for org-visible documents. ZDR and residency apply to guest data. The org membership cap defaults to 100 and would count guests unless modelled separately. Link invites are a mass-exposure path: short TTL, max uses, admin revoke, rate limit.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Add a decision gate before building: choose the guest identity model (separate principal type versus restricted org role) and write the cross-org identity and privacy contract the UI research doc requires. Make one writer own room membership (see F-t1-054 source tagging) or give guests their own subject_type excluded from the Application declarative sync. Reuse the Better Auth invitation for the email path (expiry is already mandatory) and add the room target; ship link or code invites as a later slice. Keep guests out of the org-room sync and out of org-visible Data Plane documents.
verevon.effortNote: L to XL: no guest primitive exists in any plane, and the work spans an identity-model decision, auth-core, a Control membership schema and sync change, Data Plane visibility treatment, billing seats and agent-audience fencing.
verevon.verdictReason: Recommendation stays valid and the org-invitation base is correctly described, but the approach omits the identity-model gate and the declarative-sync clobber, and underestimates effort; keep it in the late wave.

title: Teams and sub-groups with source-tracked membership; mentionable groups
summary: Add a team concept to Control (owners, members, visibility) where a team grant expands into room memberships tagged with their source, so removing someone from a team removes only team-derived grants. Later add team-level mentions (server-side expansion at send) once Space notifications exist.
whyItMatters: Teams are the core of the Teams half of the vision: orgs organise people into teams with their rooms. Today there is no team concept, only flat org membership and per-room lists. Teams are also the prerequisite for SCIM group sync, team-level agent context and group-based agent access.

others: qm (team contributes read-only resources to a turn only under a membership rule)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: teams 2 of 5 (teams, qm), mentionable groups 2 of 5 (teams, slack); common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: team(id, org_id, name, visibility), team_members(team_id, principal, role owner|member), team_rooms(team_id, room_id). Joining a team grants membership in its standard rooms; private rooms keep their own roster. Mentions: the server expands @tag into the member list at send and fans out through the notification service with per-recipient permission checks. QM teamsForTurn includes a team layer only if the actor is on the team AND the room is configured for it.

evidence: apps/Application Plane/conversation-core/conversation-core-go/internal/http/server.go:92 (ticket teams are support routing only)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/schema.ts:556-562 (comment anticipates team rooms as kind room, but no team table)
verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No team or sub-group concept, no source tracking on memberships, no group mentions; Space events produce no notifications, so group mentions have nothing to ride on.

approachOriginal: Control Plane (org-core and user-core): teams as a membership source; a team grant expands into space_memberships rows tagged with source, and removal only clears that source. Application Plane: team directory projection and, later, tag definitions; notification-core allowlist extended for mention events. Team resources reach agents only through owner-plane grants, never widened by team membership. Agents in a mentionable group must be opt-in.
risks: Team-derived plus manual membership needs source tracking or removing someone from a team will wrongly remove a manual grant. Broadcast mentions to agents can trigger many paid model turns.

verevon.exactGap: No usable team concept exists, but there is dormant scaffolding (SRC): auth-core defines team and team_member tables plus invitation.team_id in its Drizzle schema, the organization plugin config does not enable teams, and nothing reads those tables; resource_grants reserves a team subject_type in its CHECK constraint while the ACL repository rejects any non-user subject ("MVP is user-only"). Room membership has no source or provenance (space_memberships has only a free-text granted_by that the Application sync overwrites), and the only sync is a declarative full replace from Application, so team-derived memberships would be revoked as stale. There are no user-groups or group mentions in the gateway, Convex or the Space UI, and a grep found no Space-originated consumer in notification-core (INF), so group mentions have nothing to ride on.
reuse: auth-core team and team_member tables (enable the Better Auth teams option) as the team store
resource_grants subject_type team slot (already allowed by the DB CHECK) for team-level resource shares
Control space_memberships plus ReplaceMemberships (add a source dimension)
Convex spaceMemberGrants intent record and syncRoomMembersForGateway
spaceAgents triggerModes (mention|group) for agent trigger semantics
verevon.constraints: Auth Core owns membership and org-core deliberately does not mount membership or policy mutations (SRC server.go:122-128), so the team store belongs in auth-core with expansion into space_memberships in user-core; the item names org-core and user-core. The membership writer must be decided first (INF from SRC repository.go:744-775 and spaceMembers.ts:243): Application declares only manual user grants with managed_subject_types [user], so any team-derived Control membership is deactivated on the next room sync unless the declaration carries it or the sync is scoped to source=manual. Team membership never widens an owner-plane ACL (ADR-0001). Notifications: Space mention delivery does not exist, so group mentions stay a later phase as the item says. Agents in a mentionable group must be opt-in because one broadcast can trigger many paid turns.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start from the existing auth-core team and team_member tables instead of a new Control concept. Decide the single writer of room membership first: either carry a source per member in the Application declaration (manual or team:<id>) or let Control own writes with a source column on space_memberships and scope ReplaceMemberships to source=manual. Use the reserved team subject_type in resource_grants for team-level sharing.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: the dormant tables save a little, but the membership-writer decision and the sync change keep it L.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real, but the claim that no team concept exists is slightly wrong (dormant auth-core tables and a reserved grant subject exist) and the plane split should name auth-core for the team store and call out the sync clobber.

title: Personal sidebar organisation: stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hide, mute, drag-and-drop, computed system sections and cross-org badges
summary: Give each user a synced sidebar preference document (stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hidden refs, mute) edited with drag-and-drop and a batch mode, plus computed system sections over the same summaries (Agent runs, Waiting for approval, Unread, Muted) that can be toggled off, and a rate-limited stale-room suggestion. Add a per-org attention summary so the workspace switcher shows cross-org badges, with keyboard switching. Ship layout changes behind a flag with a switch-back.
whyItMatters: Sidebar organisation is table stakes in four references and becomes necessary as soon as directory, DMs and team rooms add more conversations per person; today the groups are fixed and unread is browser-local.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (sections), slack (workspace rail); Buzz (sort per group, synced sections and stars, dnd-kit sorting, More-unread pill); Teams for computed system sections and switch-back
others: Grok Bot (hide from sidebar, batch move/hide/delete for agents)

The item's 'unread is browser-local' premise is imprecise: the per-room marker is server-side in Convex, but sidebar unread dots come from a browser store populated only for rooms whose page was opened this session, and no cross-room or cross-org unread or attention aggregate exists.
reuse: ChatSidebarOrganizer native drag-and-drop with the accessible Move menu, and its zod-typed ChatOrganizationAction reducer, promoted to a server-synced preference document (this removes the 'no drag-and-drop library' concern)
listOrganizations and switchActiveOrganization behind the existing WorkspaceSwitcher for the cross-org list
activity-grammar.ts salience classes as the existing basis for a priority sort and computed system sections
Convex own-row, refs-only pattern (spaceReadMarkers, spacePresence) for the per-user preference document
server-pinned thread flag already relayed by the presentation route and the sidebar unread dot component
verevon.constraints: Each gateway request resolves exactly one authorised org (authorized_org_id from the active org), so cross-org badges need a deliberate multi-org read path that checks membership per target org and never mixes two orgs' data in one response (tenant and ZDR partition). Hide, mute and sort are presentation only and must never widen or narrow Space access; mute must be a notification preference distinct from agent pause. The preference document should store spaceRefs and ids, not room names, and live in the Application Plane as a per-user own-row record. Any server-computed attention summary must come from Application-owned read markers plus owner-plane events or APIs (approvals live in Model Plane), not DB reads. Solid 2.0 RC means prefer the existing native-drag pattern over a new library. The doc non-goals mention notification polish, which makes mute and system sections the least contentious part.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: unread is server-backed per room, so the missing dependency is a per-user, per-org attention summary (rooms with unread, waiting approvals), not 'server-side unread state'. First slice: stars, custom sections, hide, mute and per-group sort for Space rooms by promoting the chat organiser's pattern and action reducer to a synced Convex preference document; computed system sections (Unread, Waiting for approval, Agent runs, Muted) on top of the attention summary; cross-org badges and Ctrl+1..9 as a separate later item that needs the multi-org read path.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for the room-organisation slice reusing the existing organiser; the attention aggregate and cross-org badges are a separate L, so bundled it is L.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial for rooms and the pattern already exists for chat; the unread premise and the drag-and-drop concern are wrong, and cross-org badges need a different dependency than the item names.

title: Agent task tracker: Needs-input state, per-task threads and unread in the Work tab
summary: Give each agent task a visible state (working, needs input, done) with a note, a task-scoped thread beside the room and per-task unread, and project it into the Space Work tab and the activity inbox. Extend the capability-core task registry with a space_ref, a thread_ref and a needs_input state, keeping agent-owned tasks distinct from human-owned list items but linkable.
whyItMatters: A human should see exactly which agent task is waiting for them, which is the Grok Bot behaviour the vision asks for. Verevon already shows runs awaiting approval, but nothing says an agent is blocked on a question or lets a person answer in a task thread.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Task {id, title, state: working|needs_input|done, note, created_at, done_at, seen_done_at}; each task has a sub-thread id; a message sent with task_id routes to the agent about that task; a panel shows unread replies and done-but-unseen tasks, and the tasks panel is asynchronous.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Per-thread orchestration todos exist, and /v1/tasks proxies the capability-core task registry (org-scoped, status filter, create, patch, cancel) with states created, assigned, blocked and completed and an assignee, but types.go has no space or thread field (the handler may store more). The Work tab lists runs and shows awaiting_approval as a critical needs-a-human state. There is no free-form Needs-input state, no per-task thread or unread, and no room-level task list.

approachOriginal: Model Plane capability-core owns task state: add space_ref, thread_ref and a needs_input substate to the task registry and pass space_ref through the /v1/tasks proxy as the cron list already does. Application Plane projects task state into the Space Work tab and the activity inbox. Frontend renders task threads beside the room and per-task unread, and reuses the Activity grammar so a waiting task reads the same in Work and Activity. Messages posted in a task thread route to the task session.
dependencies: Adoption plan S4.5 unified Work cockpit
risks: Overlap with Lists (F-t1-058 (R-t1-08-06)); keep agent-owned tasks separate from human-owned list items and link them by ref. The task registry semantics (types.go describes a seeded catalog) need confirming.

verevon.exactGap: A durable task registry already exists (capability-core TasksHandler over the tasks table: run_id, kind, title, assignee, priority and a free-form status that PATCH accepts, produced by the cron sweeper and the API, proxied by model-gateway /v1/tasks), but it is org-scoped with no space_ref or thread_ref, no Control decision on read or write, no agent-run producer, no caller in verevonv3, and no needs-input state or agent pause to feed one; the internal/tasks/types.go the item cites is only a seeded read-only catalog. The Work tab (SpaceWorkPanel) lists runs and schedules with awaiting_approval as its only needs-a-human state, per-thread todos live in session-core, and unread is a room-level last-read marker rather than per-task.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/workplane_apis.go:768-800 (PATCH accepts any non-empty status or assignee)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/cron/sweeper.go:244 (only internal producer of task rows)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/tasks/types.go:1-30 (seeded read-only catalog, no space or thread field)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs:345-347,5341-5360 (task proxy forwards org_id and status only)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:2399-2450 (gRPC CreateTask and ListTasks proxy to capability-core)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/migrations/0004_tasks_cron_hooks_skills_memory.sql:17-40 (tasks table: run_id, status text, no space column)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-unread.ts:23-45 (unread vs a room read marker)
apps/Model Plane (grep: no needs_input, input_required or ask-user pause anywhere; no /v1/tasks caller in verevonv3 src or gateway)
reuse: capability-core tasks table and TasksHandler (status is free text, so a needs_input value needs no migration; run_id already links a task to a run, its thread and Space)
session-core threads and runs carrying Space context, so a task thread can be an ordinary Space thread created under a Control thread decision
session-core todos and plans for per-thread task steps
activity-grammar RUN_STATUS and buildSpaceWork plus SpaceWorkPanel gap rendering
Convex space read marker for unread
gateway run_watchers for notify-when-finished
verevon.constraints: Task rows are org-scoped and the list is not filtered by Space authority, so adding a free space_ref column that any org caller can set or read would leak private rooms; follow the Space cron pattern (Control decision on create, space_ref only as a filter, never a grant) or derive the Space from run_id through Session Core, and project to the Work tab only after a Space read decision. State stays in the Model Plane and Application Plane only projects it. A real needs-input state needs a Model-side clarification pause that does not exist, so this is not a frontend-only change. ZDR runs must not persist task content.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword to: link tasks to runs and threads through run_id plus a Control-bound space_ref, add needs_input as a status value together with a Model-side ask-the-human pause, and reuse the Space thread of the run and the existing todos before inventing per-task threads. Keep agent-owned tasks separate from human Lists (F-t1-058) and link by ref. Remove the quick-win label.
verevon.effortNote: Was M and a quick win. There is no agent producer, no Space authority on tasks and no clarification pause, so L.
verevon.verdictReason: The cited file is a seeded catalog; the live registry is different and more capable, but it has no Space authority. The item should say what exists (registry, status text, run link) and place the real work on authority and the pause primitive.

title: Artifact sharing: edit role, Space-as-subject grants, general access and access requests
summary: Extend the single resource_grants authority in Control Plane user-core with an edit role, a Space subject type (evaluated as the Space decision intersected with the resource grant), a general-access setting that defaults off per org, and an access-request flow with a human-only approve action. Extend ShareDialog to cover canvases, files and artifacts, not just documents. Phase 1 (edit role plus Space subject) must land together with the canvas and file library.
whyItMatters: Every artifact type in a room needs its own grants so sharing into a Space never widens the owner ACL, and the access-request loop routes the decision through a human owner. Without an edit role other members cannot co-author the canvas.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (SRC): Google-Docs-style dialog with request access and approve or decline from chat after an owner/manager check
others: Slack canvas sharing (DOC): view/edit grants independent of conversation membership, mentions notify only people with access
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grant rows {resource, subject (user|group|space), role (view|edit), granted_by}; a general_access enum on the resource; request_access creates a pending item delivered to the owner; the decide endpoint verifies the decider manages the resource's home scope, then grants (never downgrading an existing higher role) or sends a deduplicated decline notice; mentions inside an artifact notify only subjects with access.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Shares are view-only and user-only: create_share hard-codes role view and subject_type user (shares.rs:114-115), the list and revoke routes are keyed to documents, and the only other surface is a shared-with-me list. There is no edit role, no group or Space subject, no general access, no access-request or approval flow, and no sharing for non-document artifacts.

approachOriginal: Control Plane user-core: add role edit, subject_type space (grant effective only when the current Space decision also allows, per the ADR intersection rule at SPACE_AUTHORITY_ADR_2026-08-13.md:64-70), a general_access field defaulting to restricted, and an access_requests table whose approve action is human-only and not model-eligible. Gateway shares.rs: generalize routes from documents/{id}/shares to resource_type and resource_id. Frontend: extend ShareDialog and deliver requests through the activity inbox (category 05). Keep resource_grants as the only grant store.
dependencies: Resource types for canvas and file artifacts (F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01), F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03))
risks: A Space-subject grant must not become an ACL-widening path. Link access conflicts with ZDR and data residency, so keep it off by default per org. Hidden dependency: F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01) and F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03) cannot safely ship without phase 1.

verevon.exactGap: Control resource_grants already supports role edit (DB CHECK, AclRepository normalizeRole, authz check returns view or edit) and reserves a team subject, so only the gateway shares.rs hard-coding of document, user and view (lines 111-115) and the document-only, view-only ShareDialog behind the ownership gate stand between the UI and an edit role; "document" is the only ownable type in resource_taxonomy.json, a space subject_type does not exist (CHECK allows user and team), and no access-request flow exists (negative grep). Blocking finding (SRC): user-core mounts POST/DELETE /authz/grant and GET /authz/grants behind requireVerifiedAuthzDelegation, which only admits GET /authz/visible and /authz/check with a v2 ZDR-bounded delegation, while the gateway signs v1 delegation for every user-core call, so the share write path is fenced off in Control today ("Disabled until verified delegation exists" in server.go). Documents already have a Space edge (documents.space_ref plus Control retrieval decision), which overlaps with a Space-subject grant for documents.
reuse: resource_grants and AclRepository (edit role, team subject slot, ListVisible and Check)
authz facade /visible and /check with the Data Plane v2 delegation clients
documents.space_ref and Control retrieval-decision for Space-bound documents (spaces.rs space_knowledge)
Control space_memberships in the same user-core database for a Space-to-member join without cross-plane access
ShareDialog, ownership-gate honesty gate and the shared-with-me list
ADR-0001 intersection rule as the evaluation contract
verevon.constraints: ADR-0001: effective access is Space decision AND recipient audience AND owner-plane authorization, and Space membership never widens a resource ACL, so a Space-subject grant must only narrow or co-require, never add an independent path (SRC). Both resource_grants and space_memberships live in user-core, so the membership join is possible in-plane, but Space privacy, entitlement, ZDR and legal-hold conditions cannot be evaluated by a visible-ids query, so the owner plane needs a Control read-time decision as retrieval already does (INF). Every new resource type (canvas, file, artifact) must be classified in resource_taxonomy.json and its Rust mirror in retrieval-engine passes a parity lint, otherwise ValidateUserGrant rejects it. The access-request approve action must be human-only: grant a Control scope that no agent or Model service principal holds. General access conflicts with ZDR and residency, so default off per org. Agents (service principals) must never gain access through a Space subject grant. Grant administration requires the owning service to prove the actor administers the resource (SRC authz_facade.go:29-33 comment).
verevon.approachAdjustment: First unblock the write path: either add a verified resource-owner delegation (owner plane proves the actor administers the resource) or a dedicated gateway-to-Control grant-admin scope, because POST/DELETE /authz/grant and GET /authz/grants are currently rejected by requireVerifiedAuthzDelegation. Then expose the edit role (Control already supports it; only shares.rs:114-115 hard-codes view), add subject_type space with a CHECK migration, classify new resource types in the taxonomy with the Rust mirror, and build access requests on the activity inbox. For documents reuse documents.space_ref rather than duplicating it with Space-subject grants. Generalize the gateway routes to resource_type and resource_id only after the owner planes for canvas and files exist.
verevon.effortNote: M to L: the grant write surface is fenced off in Control and needs a new reviewed delegation mode, the taxonomy has a Go/Rust parity lint, and Space-subject evaluation needs a Control read-time decision. Drop the quick-win flag.
verevon.verdictReason: Premise "shares are view-only" is incomplete: the edit role already exists in Control and the real blocker is the disabled grant write surface; Space-as-subject partly duplicates documents.space_ref. Keep, but re-scope and raise effort.

title: Typed room records and Lists: one revisioned work-object substrate with a table view, assignees and item threads
summary: Build a generic Space record primitive (stable id, namespaced type, body, prev-revision CAS, idempotent resubmit) in the Application Plane, then ship Lists on top of it: typed columns, a table view first (board later), assignees, saved views and an item thread. Agents create and update records through a Model Plane tool that proposes, with authority-bearing fields staying human-only.
whyItMatters: Slack and Teams both give rooms lists, and a list is the natural place to assign work to humans and agents and see status, which is the core of humans and agents cooperating on work. One substrate avoids building tasks, decisions and checklists separately and keeps edits out of chat unread counts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack Lists (DOC) for the user model; Buzz NIP-AR (SRC) for the record substrate
others: Teams Lists, Planner and Wiki tabs (REA)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: lists: 3 of 5, common; typed-record substrate: 1 of 5, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Record = full snapshot {id (stable UUID), home_space, type (namespaced), title, body JSON, op (create|update|move|delete|restore), prev revision, optional root thread}; tables heads(id to head) and revisions; head advance is an atomic CAS on prev; resubmitting an accepted revision is idempotent; revisions never count toward unread or notifications; read access equals the room decision. A list is a record collection with a column schema {name, type: text|select|people|date|checkbox}; views store filter, sort, group and an optional default flag; assignment emits an activity item to the assignee; add message to list copies a message ref into an item.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No Space-scoped record type, list or board. Planner documents in Convex are keyed by a legacy workspaceId (an ADR resource-local partition) and orchestration todos are per thread. Tickets are a separate route unlinked from Spaces. Humans cannot edit tasks in the room and there are no assignees, views or item threads.

approachOriginal: Application Plane (Convex) owns space_records and space_record_revisions keyed by spaceRef with a registered schema per record type and prev-CAS; Control read and write decisions gate every query and mutation. Do not create another generic project authority (ADR row 84 treats the Convex projects table as a migration candidate), so records hang off the Space aggregate. Frontend: Lists tab in SpaceCockpit, table view first, board later. Model Plane: list read and update tools calling the Application API under the run's delegated decision. Assignment events feed the planned activity inbox; allow linking a ticket ref into a list item.
risks: Scope creep toward a full Planner; ship one table view and a few field types first. Generic schemas drift, so keep a registry of record types shared by UI and agent tools.

verevon.exactGap: No Space-scoped record, list or board exists: convex-core has no space_records tables (the Space tables are spaces, bindings, lifecycle, deletion, grants, readMarkers, audiences, presence), spaces.rs routes 649-731 have no records route, and the cockpit tabs are chat, work, knowledge, activity, agent, members. Only adjacent scaffolding exists: plannerDocuments (workspaceId-keyed BlockSuite metadata with no gateway or frontend consumer), thread-scoped Model Plane todos (todo.rs; read-only in the chat run panel with a status-update proxy), org-scoped capability-core /api/v1/tasks, and support tickets with saved ticket-views. The item's agent-write path is not a simple tool: Control currently supports exactly one agent owner action (tickets.create), so a records write is a new owner-action vertical.
reuse: Convex spaceRef-keyed projection pattern with service key plus requireGatewayMember (spaceReadMarkers.ts, spacePresence.ts, spaces.ts setInstructionsForGateway)

Control effect-policy pattern for new record read and write effects: a deny-by-default *_entitled column on space_effect_policies plus a decision issuer in user-core/internal/spaces (migrations 019-028)
Model Plane Todo state vocabulary (pending, in_progress, blocked, completed, cancelled; blocked_by; assignee user or agent) as the item status model
ticket-views saved-view routes in tickets.rs as the shape of saved views
activity-grammar.ts verb/object/outcome grammar for record-change rows in the Space Activity tab
SpaceCockpit tab list as the host for a Lists tab
verevon.constraints: Convex does not evaluate Space roles (spaces.ts says Space roles are not a Convex-tracked concept; the gateway verifies live Control membership and Convex only re-verifies org membership with the service key), so 'Control decisions gate every query and mutation' must be implemented as gateway-side Control decisions for new record read/write effects, not inside convex-core. Records are content, so the new table must join the Space deletion owner-receipt flow and the ZDR rule, unlike presence and read markers which are content-free. ADR rows 84-85 forbid a second generic project authority and treat planner workspaceId as a resource-local partition, so records must hang off spaceRef and not reuse plannerDocuments, workspaceId or the Convex projects table. Assignees must be Control subject ids (space_memberships allows user and service subjects); ticket or document links must be refs whose access is rechecked by the owner plane on read, since Space access never widens an owner ACL. Model proposes, owner executes: an agent may only propose record changes, and Control resolves a single supported owner action today (model_action_view.go), with the browser Model allowlist still empty.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Ship human-edited records first (table view, typed columns, assignees, saved views, per-record thread later) with gateway-side Control decisions, and take the agent create/update path out of this item: it needs a new owner-action vertical (schema hash, run-bound decision with payload digest, owner verifier, approval continuation) like tickets.create. Reuse the Todo status vocabulary instead of inventing a new one, register the table in the Space deletion flow, and keep authority-bearing fields human-only.
verevon.effortNote: L holds only for the human-edited table, assignees and saved views; the agent write path is a separate L-to-XL vertical blocked on the S2 owner-action framework, so bundling it makes this XL.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is absent (confirmed in schema, route table and cockpit tabs), but the approach misstates how agents write records and where Space authority is enforced, and bundles an owner-action vertical into a table feature.
